title: Human-in-loop canary scripts and ops storyboard (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working storyboard for running canaries that incorporate human review as a safety gate for LLM-driven features (rerankers, assistive text, content moderation heuristics). Focus: operational flow + telemetry contracts + handoff scripts so cross-functional teams can run small-batch exposures with a clear human-in-the-loop (HITL) circuit breaker.

Context / background notes (quick):
- We frequently need a human safety funnel when new model variants or prompt families are released (esp. generative + external-facing).
- Automated metrics (F1, perplexity, latency) are necessary but insufficient; we need a pragmatic micro-review loop for subjective failure modes.
- This doc aims to be lean: an ops playbook + collection of short scripts/messages + a telemetry contract for teams to wire up.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Small-batch canary with human reviewers (0.5% -> 5% exposure patterns)
- Telemetry contract (signals to emit, structured events)
- Review UI/UX sketch and minimal reviewer checklist template
- Escalation and rollback scripts for on-call and product owners
- Lightweight sampling & bias controls

Non-goals:
- Full auditor/compliance workflow for regulated customers (separate private-deployments doc)
- Long-running user studies or ML lab evaluations

Assumptions:
- Canary traffic can be tagged via route header: X-Exposure-Canary: hil-v1
- Reviewers have access to a simple review board (internal Slack threading + small web UI)
- Console emits the telemetry contract described below before reviews are shown

Success metrics (primary + safety):
- Safety pass rate (human approved / human reviewed) >= 98% for 24h window
- Escalation rate (human flagged items / human reviewed) < 0.5% baseline for safe models
- Latency P95 under canary path < 300ms added (goal)
- Cost delta per token during canary within expected budget (alert if >20% deviation)
- Coverage: 80% of sampled requests include enough context for reviewer (no truncated inputs)

Telemetry contract (required events & fields):
- event: canary.request.received { request_id, user_id_hash, canary_tag, model_name, model_version, route, timestamp, truncated_flag }
- event: canary.inference.response { request_id, latency_ms, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, beam_score? (if available), fallback_reason (if used) }
- event: canary.review.queue.added { request_id, reviewer_hint_tags, priority }
- event: canary.review.submitted { request_id, reviewer_id, outcome: [approve|flag|block], category_tags: [safety|factual|policy|toxicity|irrelevant], comment }
- event: canary.escalation.created { request_id, escalation_tier, created_by, link_to_issue }
- event: canary.rollback.triggered { rollout_id, reason, triggered_by }

Notes on PII and hashes: user_id must be one-way hashed (sha256) and not reversible. Avoid shipping raw content to analytics; only store snippet hashes for dedup checks.

Sampling & routing heuristics:
- Start with deterministic small bucket: user_id_hash % 200 == 0 (0.5% users) for 48 hours.
- If safety pass rate is strong and ops capacity exists, ramp to 2% with rule: user_id_hash % 50 in [0..1] and include targeted cohorts (new signups, power users) as separate slices.
- Prefer slow ramp with orthogonal slices so we can detect cohort-specific failure modes (mobile vs web, region, language).
- Keep an orthogonal control: route 1% to baseline model at all times for A/B measurement.

Human review funnel (operational flow):
1) Auto-checks run (toxicity heuristic, profanity regex, high hallucination-score) -> if pass, still sampled for review at lower probability.
2) If auto-checks fail or sample flagged, create review ticket and surface in "Canary Review Board" UI + #canary-review Slack channel.
3) Reviewer triages: Approve / Flag / Block. If Flag, add category tag and short rationale.
4) If Block or repeated Flags cross threshold (see gating), create escalation (Pager + Jira) and pause exposure slice.

Reviewer checklist (one-line per item, keep minimal):
- Does output contain obviously harmful or disallowed content? (yes/no)
- Is the response factually wrong in a safety-sensitive way? (yes/no)
- Any PII leakage? (yes/no)
- User intent appears benign? (yes/no)
- Quick judgement: Approve / Flag / Block + 1-sentence note

Gating thresholds (operators and PO):
- Immediate pause: if 3 Blocks in rolling 1-hour window OR 0.2% of reviewed items are Block over 1k reviews -> pause slice and notify oncall + PO
- Auto-slow: if Flags > 1% of reviewed items -> reduce exposure by 50% and open incident investigation
- Escalation to sec/legal: any PII leak confirmed OR suspected regulated data exposure

Reviewer capacity and shift planning:
- Initial canary expects ~200 reviews/day at 1% exposure for active endpoint -> requires 2 dedicated reviewers (4-6h/day) + 1 backup on-call
- Template rota: reviewer-of-the-day posts daily summary to #canary-review at 09:30 PT

UI / low-fi sketch (describe):
- Left: request context and prompt (first 500 chars) with "show full" toggle
- Middle: model output with highlightable spans; quick buttons: Approve / Flag / Block
- Right: telemetry sidebar with: model_version, latency, tokens, similarity-score to training examples (if available), auto-check flags that triggered
- One-click create-escalation -> opens pre-populated Jira with request_id + attached artifacts

Slack & oncall scripts (copy-paste):
- Slack message (for reviewer flag):
  "[CANARY FLAG] model=redwood-phi-v2 request={request_id} flagged by @{reviewer} category={category} short={one_line_comment} link={review_ui_link}"
- Oncall escalation starter message:
  "[CANARY ESCALATION] auto-pausing canary hil-v1 due to {reason}. PO @{po} and SRE @{oncall} please join. Key events: {top3_request_ids}. Link: {incident_link}. Immediate ask: triage within 30m."

Rollback & reversion play (ops steps):
1) Pause exposure (route rule -> weight 0) via console (link + audit log)
2) Trigger rollback event (emit canary.rollback.triggered)
3) Open incident in JIRA with template (below) and assign PO + SRE + Reviewer lead
4) Reproduce locally and collect top 10 flagged requests with full context (redact PII) and attach to ticket
5) Decide: model tweak, prompt update, pre-filtering, or full revert

Jira ticket template (one-paragraph):
- Summary: [CANARY PAUSE] hil-v1 exposure paused due to {reason}
- Body: include timeframe, slice selector, top flagged request_ids (redacted), telemetry links, reviewer notes, suggested immediate mitigation (revert vs prompt-block).

Quick checklist for release engineers (before enabling HIL canary):
- [ ] Telemetry events wired and validated in dev (use synthetic requests)
- [ ] Review UI reachable and permissions set for reviewers (SAML group: canary-reviewers)
- [ ] Slack channel #canary-review exists and webhook integration working
- [ ] Reviewer rota assigned and communication plan sent
- [ ] Rollback playbook link pinned in channel and runbook acknowledged by oncall
- [ ] Cost guardrail thresholds configured in Console (alerting rule)

Open questions / tradeoffs (to decide with product + SRE):
- How much of the full user prompt should be shown to reviewers vs redacted for privacy? (balance necessary context vs privacy risk)
- Do we surface model hidden scores (e.g., hallucination classifier confidence) in UI? Might bias reviewer decisions.
- Can we automate triage with a lightweight classifier to reduce reviewer load (future)?
- How to integrate external customer-managed reviewers for private deployments? (separate doc)

Next steps / action items (owner names):
- Aisha: wire a synthetic telemetry emitter for dev (due 2026-01-15)
- Marco: prototype Review Board UI (MVP: Approve/Flag/Block) and Slack integration (due 2026-01-30)
- Priya: draft reviewer rota + training one-pager (due 2026-01-20)
- Ethan: add console alert rules for cost/latency/gating thresholds (due 2026-01-22)

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Keep reviewer checklist minimal; long forms kill throughput.
- Consider an "investigate" label vs blocking to capture ambiguous cases.
- We should log reviewer decision latency (time from queue add -> submitted) to detect overloads.
- If we see high false positive flags from reviewers, run a calibration session (30m) with examples.

References and related docs:
- link: product/console-and-rollouts/fast-fallback-observation-scripts-for-llm-rollouts-wip.json (for fallback patterns)
- link: product/private-deployments/regulatory-aware-ab-canary-gating-draft.json (privacy-regulated notes)

If you're reading this and want to run a canary with HITL: ping me (Aisha) or open JIRA-1247 and add yourself to collaborators. This doc will get refined as we run the first small-batch experiment.

-- end of storyboard (WIP)
